stem: Which statement best describes glycolysis with respect to oxygen requirement and cellular location in eukaryotes?

options.label: A
options.text: It requires molecular oxygen in the mitochondrial matrix
options.explanation: Oxygen is the terminal acceptor of the electron transport chain, not a glycolytic substrate.

options.label: B
options.text: It does not use oxygen directly and occurs in the cytoplasm
options.misconception: None; glycolysis is anaerobic and cytosolic.
options.explanation: OpenStax states glycolysis is termed anaerobic and takes place in the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells.

options.label: C
options.text: It occurs only on the inner mitochondrial membrane
options.misconception: Misplaces the pathway on the ETC membrane.
options.explanation: Inner-membrane complexes belong to oxidative phosphorylation.

options.label: D
options.text: It is strictly aerobic and mitochondrial
options.misconception: Opposite of the actual oxygen independence and location.
options.explanation: Glycolysis proceeds without direct O2 use in the cytosol.

options.label: E
options.text: It occurs in the nucleus during S phase
options.explanation: Nucleotide metabolism is separate from glycolytic sugar cleavage.

context: Learning objective: place glycolysis as anaerobic cytoplasmic metabolism.
imageCaption: Cellular respiration: glycolysis -> pyruvate -> acetyl-CoA -> citric cycle carriers -> ETC/ATP synthase; O2 terminal acceptor; fermentation regenerates NAD+.
